title: Aviemore Power Station
note: Four 55 MW units, up to 220 MW; generators the largest in NZ by size (rotors nearly 8 m, 210 t); earth and concrete dam; 7 m penstocks; approved October 1962; construction 1962, fully operational 1968; mid-Waitaki scheme with Benmore and Waitaki.

title: Benmore hydro station
note: Six 93 MW units, up to 552 MW (before the July 2026 reassessment); on Lake Benmore, NZ's largest artificial lake; NZ's largest earth dam; approved October 1957 with the Cook Strait cable; built from 1958; lake filled December 1964; first power January 1965.

title: Hydro stations
note: Waitaki hydro scheme: eight stations; Meridian owns and operates Aviemore, Benmore, Waitaki and Ōhau A, B and C; Genesis Energy owns and operates Tekapo A and B. Manapōuri is NZ's largest hydro station.

title: Lake levels
note: Lakes Pūkaki, Ōhau, Ruataniwha, Benmore, Aviemore, Waitaki, Manapōuri and Te Anau; flows in the Waitaki River below Benmore, Aviemore and Waitaki dams; Lakes Te Anau and Manapōuri supply Manapōuri.

title: Manapōuri Power Station
note: Seven 128 MW units; operating maximum 800 MW (consent), 850 MW maximum continuous rating with the second tailrace; cavern about 200 m below Lake Manapōuri (West Arm), Fiordland National Park; built from 1964 by about 1,800 workers over eight years; first power September 1969; fully operational 1972; second tailrace 1998–2002; tailraces to Deep Cove, Doubtful Sound.

title: Ōhau A Power Station
note: Four 66 MW units, up to 264 MW; at the end of the Pūkaki canal where it meets the Ōhau canal; third station of the Upper Waitaki scheme; construction 1971, fully operational 1979; Lake Ruataniwha rowing course.

title: Ōhau B hydro station
note: Four 53 MW units, up to 212 MW; twin of Ōhau C; water from Lake Ruataniwha into the Ōhau C canal; construction 1977, fully operational 1984.

title: Ōhau C Power Station
note: Twin of Ōhau B; four 53 MW units, up to 212 MW; outflow to Lake Benmore; construction 1979, fully operational 1985, the last station of the Waitaki scheme.

title: Waitaki Power Station
note: Seven 15 MW units, up to 105 MW; Depression make-work project, dug by pick and shovel; first two units 1935, three more 1940–49, last two 1952–54; $440–510 million upgrade to 120 MW, due by 2036.

title: About the Waitaki hydro scheme
note: Eight stations from Lake Tekapo to Lake Waitaki, six run by Meridian from Twizel; Waitaki dam begun 1928; Aviemore (1968) completed the mid-Waitaki scheme; Upper Waitaki 1968–85; 1999 Meridian assigned the scheme; 2011 Tekapo A and B sold to Genesis Energy.

note: Opuha Dam Partnership formed 1992; construction from 1995; breach 6 February 1997; officially opened 7 November 1998; about ten years after it began operating the farmer irrigators bought the scheme outright and are now 100% shareholders of Opuha Water Ltd; a single hydro turbine, all water released generates.

title: Electricity retailer brings cheaper power to the people (Talla Burn opening release, 29 July 2011)
note: Talla Burn Generation Limited's privately developed and owned run-of-river scheme on the Talla Burn, Beaumont Station, 20 km from Millers Flat; opens 29 July 2011; the Paul Wilson Station; will generate 2.4 MW.

title: 'Bittersweet' day as power station opens
note: Opened July 2011 near Beaumont; powerhouse named the Paul Wilson Station; owned by the Hore and Wilson families; generating since November (2010).

title: Private Development of the Paul Wilson Station in New Zealand
note: 2.3 MW; commissioned September 2010, officially opened July 2011; 12 GWh a year predicted, 14 GWh in the first year.

title: Our history
note: Highbank approved 1937, generating 8 June 1945; decision to build Montalto August 1978, construction from January 1981, Montalto generating June 1982. More for the history round.

title: Ashburton Electric-Power Board, Montalto Hydro-Electric Development (project sign; photo in a historical Facebook post)
note: Seen as a screenshot sent by the Elenz team, without the post's address: head 7.3 m, maximum flow 31 m3/s; Tampella (Finland) horizontal tube turbine, 159 rev/min; Strömberg (Finland) induction generator, rated output 1,900 kW, 3,300 V; supplied by ASEA Electric (NZ); civil engineers Morris and Wilson. A lead until the post (or another public copy) can be cited.

title: Hinemaiaia hydro power scheme
note: Hinemaiaia River, Waikato; commissioned 1952–1982; max 7 MW; 30 GWh; built to supply Taupō; three stations, Hinemaiaia A, B and C; trout trap and transfer above the Hinemaiaia B dam.

title: Kuratau hydro power station
note: Kuratau River, Waikato; commissioned 1962; max 6 MW; 28 GWh; two substations, the Kuratau substation shared with The Lines Company and The Lines Company's own; boat ramp at Lake Kuratau.

title: Piriaka hydro power station
note: Whanganui River, Manawatū-Whanganui; commissioned 1924; max 1 MW; 7 GWh; built to supply Taumarunui borough; a second powerhouse with a horizontal Kaplan turbine built in 1971 doubled its output.

title: Mokauiti hydro power station
note: Mokauiti Stream, Waikato; commissioned 1963; max 1.9 MW; 7 GWh; upstream of Wairere; head 42.7 m; passive fish passage.

title: Wairere hydro power station
note: Mokau River, Waikato; commissioned 1925; max 4.3 MW; 17 GWh; downstream of Mokauiti; head 19.6 m.

title: Asset Management Plan 2026 (1 April 2026 – 31 March 2036)
note: The 2026 AMP, at an address with 2023 in it. Section 2.4: six third-party hydro stations over 1 MW, all run of river. Table 5 (p. 45): at Ōngarue GXP Kuratau 1 and 2 (3.0 MW each) and Piriaka 1–3 (1.0, 0.3, 0.3), King Country Energy; at Hangatiki GXP Wairere 4 and 5 (3.0, 1.2) and Mokauiti 1 and 2 (1.0, 0.6), King Country Energy, and Mangapēhi 1 and 2 (1.5 each) and Speedys Road 3 (2.2), Pioneer Energy. Ōngarue's generation can be switched to National Park or Tokaanu; Hangatiki's (except Speedys Road) to Whakamaru on a limited basis. Mangapēhi, Wairere Falls and Speedys Road 9.45 MVA in the Northern network.

title: King Country Energy submissions to the Proposed Waitomo District Plan (22 December 2022)
publisher: King Country Energy (via Waitomo District Council)
note: KCE owns four schemes: Kuratau (6 MW, 28 GWh), Mokauiti (1.7 MW, 7 GWh), Piriaka (1.3 MW, 7 GWh), Wairere (4.6 MW, 18 GWh), and Mangahao; embedded in the local network; Manawa operates them (major shareholder from 2016). Mokauiti: proposed by the Wairere Electric Power Board 1958, generating from 1963, 1.9 MW, two turbines, 520 m penstock, earth dam 10 m. Wairere: generating since 1925, dam since the 1950s, 4.3 MW, 17 GWh, weir above a 19 m waterfall, powerhouse about 50 m below it.

title: Mangapehi Power Scheme
note: Read in the built-in browser. Gorge on the Mangapehi River about 30 km south of Te Kuiti; commissioned 1996; head 105 m; 2,000 l/s; 5.1 GWh a year; originally The Lines Company's; 2.46 km of mainly above-ground steel pipe; two generators; connected to The Lines Company's network.

title: Speedy's Road Power Scheme
note: Read in the built-in browser. Te Anga, about 30 km west of Te Kuiti, on the Tawarau River near Marokopa Falls; commissioned 2011; head 40 m; 7.7 GWh a year; originally The Lines Company's.

title: Sale of hydro assets confirmed (20 July 2021)
note: Read through search results. TLC sold its three small hydro plants (Te Anga and Mangapēhi in Waitomo District, and Matawai near Gisborne) to Southern Generation Limited Partnership for $15.5m; sale completed Monday 19 July 2021.

title: Consent granted for local King Country hydro scheme (2018)
note: Read through search results. The Mangapēhi scheme is one of three low-impact schemes owned by TLC (the others at Matawai and Speedies Road, Te Anga); low weirs, buried pipelines, small powerhouses, no dams or storage lakes; fish passes at all three.

title: Pioneer Energy Acquires 100% Ownership Of Southern Generation (May 2024)
note: Read through search results. Pioneer Energy (owned by Central Lakes Trust) takes full ownership of Southern Generation Limited Partnership, formerly half Pioneer's and half Roaring Forties Energy LP's (The Power Company and Electricity Invercargill).

title: Tongariro Power Scheme
note: Three stations: Tokaanu (1973), Rangipō (1983) and Mangaio (2008, about 2 MW); water from the Wahianoa aqueduct passes through the 1.4 km Mangaio Tunnel under the Desert Road to Mangaio Power Station or a drop structure into Lake Moawhango via the Mangaio Stream; Genesis Energy.

title: Rivers, lakes & rainfall
note: Read through search results. Tongariro Power Scheme: water passes through pipes, lakes, canals and tunnels to the Mangaio, Tokaanu and Rangipō hydro power stations before entering Lake Taupō.

title: Kuratau Power Station
note: Western side of Lake Taupō; dam forms Lake Kuratau; proposed by Lloyd Mandeno for the King Country Electric Power Board (1952); licence 1955; operated by Trustpower for King Country Energy; Wikidata Q62004824.

title: Piriaka Power Station
note: Whanganui River near Taumarunui; Wikidata Q62415231. Not read in full (the API refused the second request).

title: Wairere Power Station
note: Mokau River above Wairere Falls; two penstocks; first unit 1925, three more 1938–1981; refurbishment 2013–2014 replaced three units with one; built by the Wairere Electric Power Board (formed January 1923); Wikidata Q85814149.
